examples.solution_text:
Find two numbers with product $-18$ and sum $-3$: $-6$ and $3$.

$\begin{align*}x^{2}-3x-18&=0\\(x-6)(x+3)&=0\end{align*}$

By the null factor law,

$\begin{align*}x-6&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x+3=0\\x&=6\quad\text{or}\quad x=-3\end{align*}$

Use PSF: product $=3\times4=12$, sum $=8$. The numbers are $2$ and $6$.

$\begin{align*}3x^{2}+2x+6x+4&=0\\x(3x+2)+2(3x+2)&=0\\(3x+2)(x+2)&=0\end{align*}$

By the null factor law,

$\begin{align*}3x+2&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x+2=0\\x&=-\frac{2}{3}\quad\text{or}\quad x=-2\end{align*}$

Recognise a difference of two squares.

$\begin{align*}(4x)^{2}-5^{2}&=0\\(4x-5)(4x+5)&=0\end{align*}$

By the null factor law,

$\begin{align*}4x-5&=0\quad\text{or}\quad4x+5=0\\x&=\frac{5}{4}\quad\text{or}\quad x=-\frac{5}{4}\end{align*}$

Take out the common factor $3x$.

$3x(2x-5)=0$

By the null factor law,

$\begin{align*}x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad2x-5=0\\x&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{5}{2}\end{align*}$

Dividing by $x$ would lose the solution $x=0$.

Rearrange so one side is zero.

$2x^{2}-5x-3=0$

Use PSF: product $=-6$, sum $=-5$. The numbers are $-6$ and $1$.

$\begin{align*}2x^{2}-6x+x-3&=0\\2x(x-3)+(x-3)&=0\\(x-3)(2x+1)&=0\end{align*}$

By the null factor law,

$\begin{align*}x-3&=0\quad\text{or}\quad2x+1=0\\x&=3\quad\text{or}\quad x=-\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$

Expand and rearrange before using the null factor law.

$\begin{align*}2x^{2}+3x-2&=3\\2x^{2}+3x-5&=0\end{align*}$

Use PSF: product $=-10$, sum $=3$. The numbers are $5$ and $-2$.

$\begin{align*}2x^{2}+5x-2x-5&=0\\x(2x+5)-(2x+5)&=0\\(x-1)(2x+5)&=0\end{align*}$

By the null factor law,

$\begin{align*}x-1&=0\quad\text{or}\quad2x+5=0\\x&=1\quad\text{or}\quad x=-\frac{5}{2}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}9x^{2}-12x+4&=0\\(3x-2)^{2}&=0\\3x-2&=0\\x&=\frac{2}{3}\end{align*}$

Both factors are $3x-2$, so there is one distinct solution.

examples.question_text: Solve $4x^{2}+20x+24=0$ by first taking out the numerical common factor.
examples.solution_text:
$4(x^{2}+5x+6)=0$

Find two numbers with product $6$ and sum $5$: $2$ and $3$.

$4(x+2)(x+3)=0$

The factor $4$ cannot be zero. By the null factor law,

$\begin{align*}x+2&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x+3=0\\x&=-2\quad\text{or}\quad x=-3\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Solve $\frac{1}{2}x^{2}+\frac{5}{6}x=\frac{1}{3}$ by first removing the fractions.
examples.solution_text:
Multiply both sides by $6$.

$\begin{align*}3x^{2}+5x&=2\\3x^{2}+5x-2&=0\end{align*}$

Use PSF: product $=-6$, sum $=5$. The numbers are $6$ and $-1$.

$\begin{align*}3x^{2}+6x-x-2&=0\\3x(x+2)-(x+2)&=0\\(x+2)(3x-1)&=0\end{align*}$

By the null factor law,

$\begin{align*}x+2&=0\quad\text{or}\quad3x-1=0\\x&=-2\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{1}{3}\end{align*}$

coverage.summary: Repaired only candidate example index 5: changed the right-hand side to 3, corrected the expansion, standard form, PSF pair, grouping and roots, and removed the numerical-factor statement and mapping. Independent derivation confirms (x-1)(2x+5)=2x²+3x-5; substituting either 1 or -5/2 into the original product gives 3. The repair follows the supplied Q5k question type and PSF teaching. All other candidate examples and assessment mappings are preserved unchanged. The baseline has no existing examples. No practice or quiz mathematics was altered or re-audited. The repaired example needs no diagram or phantom equals gutter; prose remains editable and solution ink inherits renderer blue. Visual capture remains a later stage. No files were written.

examples.derivation: The numbers -6 and 3 have product -18 and sum -3. Expanding (x-6)(x+3) gives x²-3x-18. The null factor law gives x=6 or x=-3.
ac=12; 2+6=8. Splitting the middle term gives x(3x+2)+2(3x+2)=(3x+2)(x+2). Thus x=-2/3 or x=-2.
16x²-25=(4x-5)(4x+5). Setting each factor equal to zero gives x=5/4 or x=-5/4. This combines the supplied difference-of-squares factorisation with the taught null factor law.
6x²-15x=3x(2x-5). Since 3 is nonzero, x=0 or 2x-5=0, giving x=5/2. Dividing by x would discard the valid zero solution.
Rearranging gives 2x²-5x-3=0. The PSF pair is -6 and 1, producing 2x(x-3)+(x-3)=(x-3)(2x+1). Hence x=3 or x=-1/2.
Expanding the original product gives 2x²+3x-2=3, hence 2x²+3x-5=0. The PSF pair 5 and -2 gives (x-1)(2x+5)=0. The roots are 1 and -5/2; substitution into (2x-1)(x+2) gives 3 for both.
Rearranging gives 9x²-12x+4=(3x-2)²=0. The repeated factor gives the single distinct solution x=2/3.
4x²+20x+24=4(x²+5x+6)=4(x+2)(x+3). The numerical factor 4 cannot equal zero, so x=-2 or x=-3.
Multiplying the entire equation by 6 gives 3x²+5x=2. Rearranging and splitting with the PSF pair 6 and -1 gives 3x(x+2)-(x+2)=(x+2)(3x-1)=0. Thus x=-2 or x=1/3.
